spec_match.rationale: All seventeen scenarios use the exact DOMException names from the explainer's error taxonomy and the verbatim messages from Chromium's sub_apps.cc (MojoResultCodeToDOMException / MojoAddResultTypeToDOMException / MojoRemoveResultTypeToDOMException / CheckPreconditionsMaybeThrow), correctly split across precondition, whole-batch, and per-app stages.

interactive.rationale: A grouped scenario selector drives a real locally-constructed DOMException (live name/message/legacy-code reads), the stage explainer, the trigger description, and a per-scenario handling snippet; a separate button runs the genuine add() call.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index promises every rejection and per-app failure with exact names/messages and stages; the page delivers the full taxonomy.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers the easily-missed distinctions: promise-resolves-with-failedApps versus promise-rejects, TypeError-from-undefined versus TypeError-from-invalid-path, and the two distinct QuotaExceededError messages.

references.rationale: Links the chromestatus entry plus the SubAppsAddResponse/SubAppsRemoveResponse spec anchors.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite records the SecurityError-without-policy and quota contracts as manual IWA-only assertions matching this page's scenarios, with runnable exposure scripts for what a hosted tab can genuinely check.

runtime_evidence.rationale: CDP drive: switched scenarios (quota-prompt showed the real constructed QuotaExceededError with legacy code 22; not-found switched the handling snippet to the failedApps-record form) and ran the real call, which surfaced the honest hosted-tab TypeError explanation; zero console errors, 0px overflow both classes.

telemetry_health.rationale: subapps-taxonomy-domexception-real asserts the constructed exception's name matches the scenario (can genuinely fail on browsers with incomplete DOMException support); the real-call fallback is asserted separately as subapps-taxonomy-fallback-honest.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only; scenario panels are paper-on-ivory with black borders; the warning strip uses accent-rose as a border colour, not as low-contrast text.

accessibility.rationale: Native labelled select with optgroups, definition lists for the exception fields, aria-labels on code panels, and a polite live region announcing each scenario switch; select and buttons keyboard-operable with visible focus.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Panels stack via auto-fit minmax grid, the select is full-width on mobile, long messages wrap with overflow-wrap:anywhere; 0px overflow measured at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x800.

openQuestions.title: Confirm the not-user-installable trigger surface
openQuestions.detail: kWebAppsNotUserInstallable's message is documented from Chromium source, but the exact profiles/platforms that produce it (managed guest sessions? off-the-record?) are described from inference. Verify against a real Chrome 152 enterprise/managed profile and tighten the trigger text.

openQuestions.title: Record real rejections from inside an IWA
openQuestions.detail: Once a sample IWA run exists (see capability-probe question), capture at least SecurityError (policy revoked) and NotAllowedError (prompt declined) genuinely and embed the recorded outcomes alongside the constructed objects.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible live region status updates aria-live button action result
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Group long option sets with optgroups on a native select and mirror selection results in a polite live region.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Native select with four staged optgroups; scenario changes and real-call outcomes announced via aria-live polite output.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive form control panel layout without horizontal overflow mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use auto-fit minmax grids so side-by-side panels stack on narrow viewports; scroll wide code blocks internally.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Exception/stage panels in an auto-fit minmax(15rem,1fr) grid; handling and shape pres overflow:auto; 0px overflow at 360px verified.

summary: Complete, stage-aware map of the Sub Apps error taxonomy with real DOMException objects, exact Chromium messages, per-scenario handling code, and a genuine call showing what a hosted tab actually does. CDP-verified in headless Chromium across both viewport classes with scenario switching and the real call exercised and zero console errors.
